assignments.brief_reason: Describes removing clearly hateful items and handling mixed-good/mixed-bad valence with deletion decisions.
Mentions checking whether statements are untrue/inane, but not explicitly tied to threat/violence exceptions or toxicity thresholds.
Removes when discussion devolves into cursing rather than constructive discussion, consistent with removing toxic/vulgar content.
Uses a healthy-debate contribution rule and uncertainty to avoid removal; not clearly threat/toxicity or free-speech-with-violence exceptions.
Uses truth-bending/side alignment to compare a pair; codebook themes don’t match this pair-comparison rationale.
Applies a bar distinguishing blatantly over-the-top/derogatory content from genuinely harmful, implying removal for toxic gradations.
Approves only when there is no profanity or dangerously worded attacks, i.e., removing toxic/profane content.
Comparatively assesses harm and may block both; aligns with high bar removal to prevent harmful/toxic content (though not explicitly about threats/violence).
Explicitly screens for anything dangerous to a group or individual, aligning with violence/threat exception logic.
Advocates posting/keeping on-topic and not picking a side, implying consistent standards across viewpoints.
Uses anticipated backlash and incitement risk to decide harder cases, consistent with removing when content becomes inflammatory/toxic.
Favors respectful, non-insulting posts and penalizes crudeness/insults, matching toxicity/threat-informed removal.
Rejects name calling/profanity and extreme personal accusations (e.g., 'cancer'), which is explicitly toxic-language removal.
Compares follow-up viability/openness vs dead ends/insults; not clearly a threat/toxicity or violence-exception criterion.
Uses harm potential (and evidence) to decide; harm focus fits the removal-for-toxicity/high-bar theme more than free-speech-with-violence exceptions.
Explicitly aims to be fair and not biased, supporting applying the same moderation standard across viewpoints.
Advocates free speech while limiting degrading 'bad-mouthing'; not specifically framed as threats/violence exceptions, but it is a free-speech-with-limit stance.
Believes misunderstanding is inevitable, shaping expectations about pairing; not tied to any moderation standard theme.
Claims both viewpoints are essential for understanding and supports free speech via showing both, implying consistent criteria across sides.
Removes when posts likely cause broad controversy; this reflects keeping a higher bar to avoid inflammatory/toxic outcomes.
